framing: Turn raw crawls into clean, deduplicated training tokens
paragraphs: Scaling laws tell you how many tokens a training run needs; data engineering decides whether those tokens teach reasoning or memorize web boilerplate. Duplicate pages, leaked benchmarks, and low-quality scrapes quietly waste millions in GPU compute.
This chapter walks through extraction, quality filtering, MinHash deduplication, domain mixing, and contamination checks that turn raw corpora into high-signal pretraining datasets.
outcomes: Design a staged pretraining data pipeline from raw text extraction through deduplication and mixing.
Measure near-duplicate rates and benchmark contamination before committing GPU hours.
question: Why does repeating a small subset of near-duplicate documents hurt generalization far more than its raw token percentage suggests?
